newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore noon stocks ease, interest in Hong Kong.
newsitem.headline: Singapore noon stocks ease, interest in Hong Kong.

text.p: The Singapore stock market eased at midday on Tuesday as institutional investors shifted interest to the Hong Kong stock market, dealers said.

"There is not much money to be made in a market that is trending sideways. It is better to put it elsewhere," said an institutional dealer with a foreign firm, citing Hong Kong as the preferred alternative.
Singapore's May non-oil domestic export figures due for release next week also kept investors sidelined, dealers said.
"We are expecting a slow down, perhaps a zero to five percent growth," said another dealer.
At 0430 GMT, the Straits Times Industrials Index eased 2.73 points to 2,027.48. Volume was light, around 52 million shares, with 132 gainers to 127 losers.
Hong Kong-based Jardine group of companies - HongKong Land, Jardine Matheson and Jardine Strategic -- was active on renewed rumours of its relisting in Hong Kong despite official denials.
"The shares and warrants are riding on that possibility," said a local dealer.
Small-capitalised stocks like fruit seller FHTK and paper product maker New Toyo hit new year highs in active trade on buy recommendations.
